answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on an attestation graph, so influence reaches a cluster only along traversed edges. If a sybil cluster has sparse external cuts and hence low conductance, little walk mass enters from honest nodes; with bounded per-node voting weight, this limits its aggregate vote. A mesa-like cluster cannot amplify trust merely by adding internal edges: a prism of independent attestations must cross the cut, while pearl denotes a single edge and contributes only limited flow.
